target_customer: Corporations and governments buying durable carbon dioxide removal credits
problem: Open-ocean seaweed could remove carbon at scale if grown and sunk cheaply; Phykos proposed solar-powered autonomous vessels to cultivate and sink it.
business_model: Sell carbon removal credits generated by autonomous seaweed cultivation vessels (per a profile; not confirmed on a company site)

founders.name: Nico Julian
previous_startups: Solar and marine satellite communications startups (names not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: mechanical engineer with marine satellite communications, solar startups and moonshot origination at Google X.

founders.name: Jeff Zerger
previous_startups: Early-hire roles at cleantech, food and aerospace startups (names not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: self-taught software engineer with about 25 years in Silicon Valley and over a decade at Apple and Google.

competitors.name: Running Tide
competitors.what: Maine startup growing kelp and sinking biomass for carbon removal
competitors.traction_then: First customer Shopify; Microsoft contract for 12,000 tons CO2 equivalent over two years announced in March 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous solar-powered ocean vessels, open-ocean cultivation and verification of sequestration with an uncertain regulatory path for a two-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and operating know-how are hard to copy, but the carbon credit market was unproven and no patents or contracts were found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No large player acquired or copied the approach; the sector's lead startup Running Tide later shut down.

market_need_then: Corporate buyers such as Microsoft and Shopify were buying carbon removal in 2021, and Phykos's launch press (Fast Company, September 2021) framed ocean seaweed as a scalable removal route.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand assets or press about the brand were found, and the Greek-derived name is hard to spell; the YC page lists no website.

outcome_analysis: Phykos is listed as active with two people and no website on its YC page, and no priced round, exit, shutdown or pivot was found in public sources. Press coverage in 2021 described a seaweed carbon removal concept still before proof of principle, in a field where Running Tide later closed. The outcome is not yet clear and funding is unknown rather than zero.
notes: No company website exists on the YC page, so there was nothing to fetch. Aggregators report about 130,000 dollars (CB Insights, round dated 2021-08-31) or 250,000 dollars (Caplight) from YC, Climate Capital, Tango.vc and Leap Forward Ventures; these come from aggregators only and are unverified, so no round is recorded. The Greek word phykos means seaweed (dictionary entry for phyco-), but no source says the founders chose it for that reason. Location listed as San Francisco on YC and Oakland by a profile. Education of founders not stated on sources opened. Competitor source is dated May 2021, within the batch year.
